message.content: lowercase with square-bracket annotations is a deliberate style choice to maximize both human scanability and machine parseability: the lowercase eliminates unnecessary visual noise (no caps-lock, no exclamation-points, no weird-quotes), letting the reader's eye glide over the text and land on the actual semantic signal, while the square-brackets serve as a lightweight metadata schema that machines can hook into for lint-checks, docgen-passes, and change-log auto-generation — `[owner: alice]`, `[deprecated: 2026-01]`, `[reason: perf]` — all in one place, so you know who touched it, why it changed, and when it expires, without bloating the line with prose. it's the difference between reading a paragraph and reading a label on a shelf: you don't need to re-read every word, you just scan the brackets, get the gist, and move on.
